_note: Each case runs one skill against a fresh copy of examples/fixture-os and then reads the filesystem. Assertions are deliberately structural -- what got written, where, and what stayed untouched -- because that is what the cross-cutting rules actually claim. Two checks run on every case regardless: raw/ stays append-only, and a usage/log.md row gets appended. The frame answers a skill's clarifying question rather than stopping at it: two cases in the first full run wrote nothing at all because corp-os-intake and corp-os-brief correctly refused to proceed without a person -- intake asks when a type is ambiguous, brief asks for a window when meta.json holds no prior brief. Both were doing exactly what their skill says. Reading that as failure would have 'fixed' two skills that were right; the harness was wrong. Cases carry an optional `fixture` -- examples/fixture-os is the shipped default shape, examples/fixture-register is a jobs-off OS with renamed vocabulary and a hand-maintained source layer. The irreversible-path cases run against the register fixture because that is where a role mistake actually costs something.

Six runs across three configurations -- the scaffolder unmentioned, the scaffolder called in Step 3, the scaffolder as Step 0 before any question -- all produced a domain-shaped folder (agreements/, renewals.md, vendors/, a template, a clause checklist) and none of the five invariants. 2/9 to 3/10 every time.

Two readings, and they are worth separating before anyone 'fixes' this again. It may be the skill: with no existing OS to anchor to and a request dense with domain content, the structure loses to the vocabulary. Or it may be this harness: the frame says 'the skill is at <path>, read it and follow it', which a model may treat as reference material rather than as the procedure it must execute. cases.prompt: Build me a stakeholder map for the renewal — who's involved and where each of them stands.
cases._note:
Third version of this case's assertion, and the first two were both wrong about the skill rather than the reverse.

v1 asserted the string 'corp-os-configure' appeared in the answer. It failed a run that declared people/ with role, entry_schema, index_line, label_field, order_by and decay, behind a written proposal citing gate.mode -- it simply never said the skill's name. Testing vocabulary, not behavior.

v2 asserted config.json changed. Two live runs took two different legitimate paths: one declared the layer and filed entries, one wrote the proposal and built the map from what already existed, leaving the declaration for the person to confirm. Asserting config.json changed picks a winner between two correct behaviors.

What both correct runs did, and what improvising a layer inline does not, is leave a proposal behind. That plus the incomplete-index check covers the failure this case exists for: a layer conjured to serve a rendering, with no review and the wrong shape.

Measured, and left failing on purpose: 2/5 runs across three rounds. One declared the layer with full shape and filed a proposal; one filed the proposal and built the view from what already existed; three built the view and mentioned the gap only in the answer, where it died with the session. A wording pass making the proposal requirement explicit was tried and measured at 0/2, so it was reverted rather than kept -- prose that does not move the number is churn, and this repo has argued that four times about other people's code. Nothing mechanical catches this one: the runs that miss it leave no dangling reference and no undeclared directory, because they infer the view from layers that do exist. Deciding a layer is warranted is judgment, which is the one thing the shipped scripts cannot take over. Recorded as an open number rather than patched a third time.

Moved in 0.25.2, and not by a third wording pass. Measured 3/3 in the first round and 2/3 in the second — 5 of 6 against 1 of 5 before, so the fix is real and the rate is not 100%. Recorded at 5/6 rather than claimed at 3/3: one round of three is how this repo talked itself into a 1/3 that was a division. The branch was already in the skill — "if the OS has no pattern for what they want, that is corp-os-pattern's job" — sitting in prose beside a numbered procedure, which is where corp-os-jobs sat at 0/3. It became `bind_pattern.py --want`, a numbered step that refuses with two answers and no third. The index_line half moved to log_run.py in 0.25.3: build_index.py already renders an "Incomplete index" banner for the defect, so a person was never the right thing to notice it.

cases._note:
fixture-os carries a Granola connector with `Verbatim fetch: yes` and one summary-fidelity entry sourced from it, plus entries whose citation is the sanctioned `no source` literal. The two populations are the whole test: one is one call from stronger, the other can never be re-confirmed, and collapsing them is the failure this release exists to fix.

The needle is `fetch` rather than a phrase I chose, because it is the word the connector record itself uses — the vocabulary mistake this suite has made three times is checking for language the run had no reason to pick.

Two things came out of running this, and they went opposite ways.

**A real defect, found and fixed.** The cross-cutting check that every derived-layer write has a proposal behind it failed on three of the first four runs — one of them rewriting fourteen files and filing nothing. corp-os-reality-check had no gate step at all, which is a serious gap in the one skill whose whole job is removing things: the declines are the valuable part of the record, and a retirement that happened in conversation and nowhere else is indistinguishable six months later from something that was never there. Step 1.5 was added, and the check went to 2/2.

**A needle that measured nothing, removed.** `fetch` in the answer scored 1/2, then 2/2, then 0/2 across three batches. That spread is a coin flip on a word choice, not a skill behaving inconsistently — a run can treat the promotion backlog as entirely actionable while writing 'pull the transcript' or 'the original is still available'. It is the fourth time this suite has checked for vocabulary and called it behaviour. The safety-critical half of the same property is kept as a forbid_output, because 'nothing was promoted without an actual fetch' is checkable and has held every run.

What is left unmeasured, and stated rather than papered over: whether the backlog is *framed* as actionable. That is a quality judgment about an answer, and this harness cannot see it.

cases.prompt: We still haven't landed on whether to keep the legacy importer or rewrite it. Can you get that into my OS?

expect_output.name: routes an undecided fork to corp-os-decide
expect_output.why: the skill's own rule is to read the tense: a choice still open is a decision record, a choice already made is a claim. Filed as anything else, nothing ever forces the date and the fork sits open for months

expect_untouched.name: guide did not open the decision itself
expect_untouched.why: guide orients and hands off; a run that does the work skips the skill that has the rules for doing it properly

expect_untouched.name: guide did not file it as a claim
expect_untouched.why: an undecided fork written as a claim is the exact misfiling this routing rule exists to prevent

expect_untouched.name: guide wrote nothing to the source layer
expect_untouched.why: routing is not capture

cases._note: The phrasing 'get that into my OS' reads like intake or claims, and the tense is the only thing that says otherwise. Assertions are on the answer and on what stayed untouched, because a routing skill's whole deliverable is the answer plus a log row.

cases.prompt: I want a dashboard for renewal risk. Add that as a job.
cases.answers: the reason I want it is that I keep finding out an account is in trouble at the QBR instead of before it

expect_added.name: a job file was written
expect_added.why: the jobs layer is enabled in this fixture and the person asked for a job; a run that only discusses the shape has filed nothing

expect_untouched.name: the dashboard they asked for was not built
expect_untouched.why: the request names an artifact; this skill converts it into an outcome rather than satisfying it. Building the dashboard here is how the malformation gets baked in instead of repaired

expect_added_contains.name: the job written carries an outcome clause
expect_added_contains.why: artifact-as-motivation is the most common malformation: 'I want a dashboard' names a thing, not a motivation, and a job with no outcome cannot be closed. The required form is `When <situation>, I want to <motivation>, so I can <outcome>`, so the clause is schema rather than phrasing — checked in the file the run wrote, not in what it said about it

cases._note: The first version asserted 'so I can' against the answer, which tested narration rather than the record. The cases file already carries one note about dropping an assertion for testing the slug a run happened to choose; this was the same mistake.

cases.prompt: Take a look at how I've been using this and tell me what to change.

expect_untouched.name: no improvement packet written from one occurrence
expect_untouched.why: a packet is the model-change deliverable and the most expensive thing to act on; writing one off a single friction row sends someone to edit the plugin over an n of 1

expect_untouched.name: no proposals written from one occurrence
expect_untouched.why: the bar is more than one real occurrence. Proposing from a single one is manufacturing findings from noise, and this skill is the most prone to it because a person who asked for changes wants changes

expect_untouched.name: improve wrote no claims
expect_untouched.why: this skill studies how the OS is used and proposes changes to it. Writing a claim means it answered a question nobody asked with material it was reviewing, and it is corp-os-claims that has the rules for doing that properly

cases._note: Asserts the refusal structurally. The first version looked for the word 'once' in the answer, which tests narration; the run that failed it had written claims/pricing.md, which is the defect worth catching and which no wording check would have named.

cases.prompt: Add a company record for Ardent Materials — what they sell, who buys it, how they price, and who they compete with.
cases.answers: yes, go ahead and add it

expect_untouched.name: no claim was written from recalled knowledge
expect_untouched.why: the skill's own Step 2 says do not answer any of the nine areas from recalled knowledge and do not present recalled knowledge as a finding. A conformance run has no search tool, so every one of them is unanswerable here — and a claim that appears anyway came from the model, with no source anyone can check, into a layer everything else in the suite trusts

expect_untouched.name: no source material was invented to cite
expect_untouched.why: the way a fabricated record passes a citation check is by manufacturing the thing it cites. This is the failure that would make every later provenance check meaningless

file_lacks.name: the company did not enter the scan path
file_lacks.why: a record that reaches INDEX.md is a record every other skill will read and believe. Asserted against the index rather than against a folder because this fixture has no company layer, so a company/ check would pass vacuously whatever the run did

cases._note: The refusal case for the one skill that cannot do its job without the network. Named a company the fixture holds nothing about, so harvesting (Step 1) has nothing to return and research (Step 2) has no tool — which leaves saying so as the only honest output. Deliberately not asserting the wording of that refusal: `improve-thin-evidence`'s first version looked for the word 'once' in the answer and passed a run that had written claims/pricing.md, which is the defect worth catching and which no wording check would have named.

cases.prompt: The review gate keeps getting skipped — I've watched runs write to a derived layer with nothing left in proposals/. Write this up as a change against the plugin so I can send it upstream.
cases.answers: I maintain the plugin myself, so skip the anonymization; go ahead

expect_untouched.name: config.json was not edited
expect_untouched.why: Step 5 names config.json specifically: the deliverable is a portable document meant to leave this OS, and a skill that reshapes the OS on its way to writing one has confused the two corpora

expect_untouched.name: the finding was not filed as knowledge
expect_untouched.why: a diagnosis about the plugin is not something the OS knows about the person's work. corp-os-claims has the citation and gate rules for anything that does belong there

cases._note:
This case exists for the cross-cutting plugin-source check rather than for anything in its own list. corp-os-contribute reads ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and writes diffs against real files, the harness runs with acceptEdits and Bash allowed, and applying one edits this repo rather than the throwaway copy — where the work/ digest would never see it. 'Never modify the plugin's own files directly from this skill, even when they're technically reachable' was asserted in prose and untestable until the harness snapshotted the plugin around every run.

The deliverable's path is deliberately not asserted. Step 5 says 'a portable document meant to leave this OS — not a write to usage/' and names no location, so pinning one would test whichever convention a run happened to choose, which this file has already been wrong about twice.

cases.prompt: This is where I keep everything. Have a look and tell me what's weak about it and what I should do — and write the audit up as a file here so I can come back to it.
cases.answers: I built it after rebuilding the same analysis twice; I use it to remember why I decided things; what annoys me is that I can't answer a question without opening five files

expect_untouched.name: the auditor did not reorganize their notes
expect_untouched.why: Step 4 is explicit: do not start converting anything unasked, an auditor who reorganizes someone's system is not welcome twice. This is the failure that makes the whole skill unusable, and it is the one a model is most tempted into because the shipped shape is right there

expect_untouched.name: the auditor did not reorganize their projects
expect_untouched.why: same rule, and asserted on a second folder because a run that tidies one and not the other has still done it

expect_untouched.name: their superseded file was left alone
expect_untouched.why: the most obviously 'wrong' file in the system, kept deliberately and for a stated reason. Deleting or merging it is the audit substituting its own judgment for a convention it was asked to assess

expect_added.name: an audit was actually written
expect_added.why: the person asked for a file they could come back to; an audit delivered only in chat ends with the session, which is the same failure the review gate exists for one corpus over

forbid_output.name: the stated deliberate omission was not recommended back
forbid_output.why: their README says they never write anything down about people and why. Step 5 calls a deliberate omission the most valuable and least obvious category to find — recommending a person layer here is the precise signature of scoring against the shipped model instead of reading what they built, which is what Step 3 is for

cases._note:
The third fixture shape: a system that is not a Corp-OS and was never meant to be. 528 tokens, no index, no config, no provenance, filename-as-index, one folder capitalized and one not.

It carries two things on purpose. A convention the shipped model has no equivalent for — every entry ends with a `How I'd be wrong` falsifier, which is what Step 5 exists to find and adopt — and a deliberate omission stated with its reason, which is what Step 5 calls the most valuable category and what the forbid_output above tests from the other direction.

Not asserting that the report NAMES the falsifier convention. The report's own text is the natural place to check it and the transcript is truncated to the last 8000 characters, so the check would fail on report length rather than on content. Recorded here rather than shipped as a flaky assertion.
